job.title: Casual Early Childhood Educators - Carindale and Surrounding Areas
job.description:
Join Expect A Star as a Casual Educator in Carindale - Australia’s most trusted early education agency, proudly supporting educators for over 20 years.

Are you looking for a rewarding role in Early Childhood Education that fits around your life? Expect a Star is currently searching for passionate Early Childhood Educators who are willing to undertake casual shifts in childcare centres in Carindale and surrounding suburbs (Thornlands, Birkdale, Wakerley and more!)

Whether you are looking to balance work with study, family commitments, or simply want to experience different learning environments, our easy-to-use app allows you to manage your own availability and choose when you work.

Benefits & Perks
  • Complete Flexibility: Set your own schedule! Work anywhere from 2 to 5 days a week based on your availability.
  • Top Pay Rates: Receive competitive, above-award casual hourly rates, paid reliably every single week.
  • Streamlined App: View, accept, and manage your shifts effortlessly through our custom casual educator app.
  • Routine & Stability: Ongoing block bookings and regular shifts are available in Carindale and Brisbane's eastern suburbs for suitable candidates.
  • National Rewards Program: Access exclusive employee discounts on retail, dining, travel, gym memberships, and health services.
  • Career Growth: Experience various teaching philosophies and open doors to potential permanent opportunities.

Key Responsibilities
  • Provide high-quality care and education for children aged 0–5 years in a safe, inclusive, and nurturing environment.
  • Assist in implementing fun, play-based educational programs in line with the EYLF.
  • Support permanent centre staff by seamlessly stepping in during busy periods, staff absences, or scheduled leave.
  • Build positive relationships with children, families, and team members.
  • Maintain excellent supervision and adhere to National Quality Standards (NQS) and health and safety regulations.

What We’re Looking For
  • Qualifications: Hold a Certificate III or Diploma in Early Childhood Education and Care (or be actively studying an ACECQA-approved qualification)
  • Compliance: A valid Queensland Working with Children Check (Blue Card) for paid employment.
  • Certifications: Current food handling certificate and GECCKO National Child Safety Certificate (or a willingness to obtain them quickly).
  • Availability: Available at least 2 days per week, with flexibility for occasional short-notice shifts.
  • Work Rights: Valid, unrestricted working rights within Australia.
  • Skills: Excellent communication, a proactive work ethic, and a genuine love for working with children.

About Expect A Star
Established in 2004, Expect A Star is a leading specialist recruitment agency dedicated to the Early Childhood Education sector. As part of the PeopleIN family—the largest talent solutions company in Australia and New Zealand - we are proud to support thousands of educators in finding flexible, fulfilling work.

How to Apply
If you are ready to take control of your work-life balance and join a supportive agency team, click "Apply Now" to submit your resume. A member of our Queensland recruitment team will be in touch

job.description:
Benefits
  • Salary of up to $120,000 per annum
  • Permanent, full-time position
  • Join a supportive, values-driven organisation focused on making a genuine difference to young people
  • Work as part of a multidisciplinary team alongside Youth Workers, Teacher Aides and Welfare staff
  • Professional development opportunities
  • Employee Assistance Program for staff and families
  • Fitness Passport available
  • PBI salary packaging through SPA, providing the opportunity to reduce your taxable income
The Role
The School we are assisting are seeking an experienced and passionate Teacher in Meadowbrook.

This is an opportunity to teach in an alternative learning environment where relationships come first and your approach can make a genuine difference to young people who have disengaged from traditional schooling.

As a Teacher, you will plan and deliver the Australian Curriculum and QCAA Curriculum across relevant year levels, using flexible, individualised and differentiated approaches to meet the needs of each student.
You will work closely with Youth Workers, Teacher Aides and the Welfare team to support students' learning, wellbeing and engagement. The role will also involve monitoring academic progress, assessment and reporting, behaviour management, pastoral care and supporting students with their future education, training and employment pathways.
The role includes 20 contact hours and 15 hours dedicated to planning, meetings and collaboration with your team.

Role Requirements
  • Bachelor of Education or equivalent teaching qualification
  • Current Queensland College of Teachers (QCT) registration
  • Proven teaching and learning experience
  • Previous experience teaching in a flexible learning or alternative education environment is highly regarded
  • Extensive understanding of the issues and barriers facing young people at risk
  • Demonstrated ability to successfully engage young people through relevant and dynamic learning
  • Experience supporting students with disabilities and an understanding of individualised learning approaches
  • Strong behaviour management skills and the ability to support students experiencing behavioural challenges
  • Ability to provide modified and differentiated instruction and targeted adjustments
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to work effectively with students, parents, school personnel, training providers and other stakeholders
  • Strong teamwork, problem-solving and organisational skills
  • Ability to work respectfully with people from diverse backgrounds and experiences
  • Current criminal history/working-with-children screening with no adverse or unsuitable findings
The School
Provides alternative learning environment designed to meet young people where they are and help them reconnect with education. The focus is on building resilience, developing personal and social skills, improving educational outcomes and supporting students towards successful future pathways.
Teachers work collaboratively with a wider support team to provide a holistic approach to education and wellbeing. The position description highlights the importance of flexible curriculum delivery, individualised learning, targeted adjustments, pastoral care and supporting students with disabilities.

If you're a teacher who is resilient, flexible, relationship-focused and passionate about helping young people re-engage with learning, this could be an excellent opportunity to make a meaningful difference.
